NotifyDeliveryReason.description:
Why a delivery was skipped, held, retried or failed. Open enum: new reasons may be added.

- `suppressed_preference`: The recipient turned this channel off for this type or its category. Fix: Nothing to fix: the recipient chose this. Mark the category channel `mandatory` only for messages they must receive.
- `unsubscribed_all`: The recipient unsubscribed from all non-critical notifications. Fix: Only types marked `critical` still reach them; otherwise the recipient has to opt back in.
- `held_quiet_hours`: Held until the recipient's quiet hours end. Fix: It is sent when the window ends. Mark the type `critical` if it must not wait.
- `scheduled_send`: Waiting for the send time given in `send_at` or `delay_seconds`. Fix: It is sent at that time. Cancel it with the notification id or its `cancellation_key`.
- `no_device`: The recipient has no active device for this channel. Fix: Register the device token from your app (`POST …/devices`) after the user grants permission.
- `no_address`: The recipient has no email address. Fix: Set `email` on the recipient, or pass it inline in the send.
- `email_invalid`: An earlier email to this address hard-bounced. Fix: Update the recipient's email address; a new address clears the bounce.
- `email_complained`: The recipient marked an earlier email as spam. Fix: Email stays off for this recipient; reach them through another channel.
- `email_paused`: Email is paused for this workspace (high bounce or complaint rate). Fix: Check your sending in the console and resume email in Notify settings.
- `email_budget`: The workspace email budget is spent for now; the email waits for the next window. Fix: It is sent automatically when the budget allows. Ask us to raise the budget if this is routine.
- `email_backlog_full`: The workspace already holds 10,000 emails waiting for budget, so this one was not queued. Fix: Send fewer emails or spread them out; ask us to raise the budget if this volume is routine.
- `channel_not_configured`: The channel is not set up in this workspace. Fix: Upload APNs or FCM credentials, generate web push keys, or enable Mail with a verified sender.
- `channel_restricted`: The send's `channels` list left this channel out. Fix: Add the channel to `channels`, or omit `channels` to use every channel of the type.
- `type_archived`: The notification type is archived. Fix: Unarchive the type or send a different one.
- `credential_invalid`: No valid credential matches this device's app or environment. Fix: Upload the APNs key or FCM service account for this bundle id or project, in the right environment.
- `template_missing`: The type has no template for this channel. Fix: Add a template for the channel (any locale) to the notification type.
- `rate_limited`: The recipient already received the per-minute maximum of notifications. Fix: Send fewer notifications to one person, or batch them; critical types have their own budget.
- `throttled`: The type's own throttle for this recipient was reached. Fix: Raise or remove `throttle` on the notification type if every message must go out.
- `read_in_inbox`: The recipient read the inbox item first, so the follow-up was not needed. Fix: Nothing to fix: this is how `after_unread_seconds` works.
- `awaiting_unread`: A follow-up step waiting to see whether the recipient reads the inbox item first. Fix: Nothing to fix: it is sent when the `after_unread_seconds` timer ends and the item is still unread, and skipped as `read_in_inbox` otherwise.
- `actor_excluded`: The recipient is the actor who caused the notification. Fix: Pass `exclude_actor: false` to notify the actor too.
- `recipient_not_found`: No recipient with this external id exists in the workspace. Fix: Create the recipient first (`PUT /recipients/{external_id}`), pass it inline with an email, or send `create_missing: true`.
- `recipient_erased`: The recipient was erased in the last 24 hours and cannot be recreated by a send yet. Fix: Wait 24 hours after the erasure, then create the recipient again.
- `mail_suppressed`: ProductCraft Mail suppressed the address (earlier bounces or complaints). Fix: Check the suppression list in Mail; remove the address only if you know it is valid.
- `mail_refused`: ProductCraft Mail refused the message (the code after the colon says why). Fix: Look up the Mail error code; usually the template name or sender needs fixing.
- `pruned`: The push provider said the device token is no longer valid; the device was removed. Fix: Nothing to fix: the app registers a fresh token the next time it opens.
- `payload_too_large`: The rendered push payload is over the provider's size limit. Fix: Shorten the template or move data out of the push payload.
- `credential_error`: The push provider rejected the workspace credential. Fix: Upload a fresh APNs key or FCM service account; the channel resumes as soon as it validates.
- `circuit_open`: The provider is failing for this credential, so sends are paused briefly and retried. Fix: Nothing to fix: it retries on its own. Check the provider's status page if it lasts.
- `expired`: The notification's time to live passed before it could be delivered. Fix: Raise `ttl_seconds` on the type if late delivery is still useful.
- `cancelled`: The notification was cancelled, or the recipient was erased, before delivery. Fix: Nothing to fix.
- `provider_error`: The provider kept failing until retries ran out. Fix: Check the attempts for the provider status and code.

info.description:
Notifications for the ProductCraft platform: one call notifies a user across an in-app inbox, email (through ProductCraft Mail), web push, APNs and FCM, with per-user preferences, fallbacks, quiet hours, templates per channel, delivery history and signed webhooks. Push to Apple and Google devices uses your own APNs key and Firebase service account, which you upload once (stored encrypted, never returned).

## Rate limits

Every `/v1` route is limited per client IP to 20 requests per second and 600 per minute. Each response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit-short`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining-short`, `X-RateLimit-Reset-short` (the one-second window) and the same three with `-long` (the one-minute window). Over either limit the response is `429` with code `RATE_LIMITED` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying with the same key (sent with `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`).

429.description: More than 20 requests per second or 600 per minute from this client IP (`RATE_LIMITED`); wait `Retry-After` seconds.
